description: Letters for numbers: terms, like terms and substitution

lessons.title: A Letter Can Stand for a Number
lessons.intro: In algebra a letter stands for a number we do not know yet, or a number that can change. The letter is called a variable.
explanation: If a pencil costs x rupees, then x could be 5, or 8, or any other price.
We can still work with x, even before we know its value.
x + 2 means 2 more than x. If x = 5, then x + 2 = 7.
lessons.rule: A variable is a letter that stands for a number.
lessons.tip: Any letter will do. x, y and n are common choices.

steps.text: Let x be the number of marbles in a bag.
If the bag had 5 marbles, put 5 in place of x.
steps.tip: With 5 marbles to begin with, there are now 7.

lessons.title: The Hidden Times Sign
lessons.intro: In algebra we do not write the × sign between a number and a letter.
explanation: 3x = 3 × x. It means three lots of x.
xy = x × y. Two letters side by side are multiplied.
The number is always written first. We write 3x, not x3.
lessons.rule: A number next to a letter means multiply.
lessons.tip: 3x is three lots of x added together: x + x + x = 3x.

lessons.title: Terms
lessons.intro: An expression is made of parts called terms. Terms are joined by plus and minus signs.
explanation: 4x + 7 has two terms: 4x and 7.
2x + 3y − 5 has three terms: 2x, 3y and 5.
To count the terms, count the parts between the plus and minus signs.
lessons.rule: Terms are the parts of an expression joined by plus or minus signs.
lessons.tip: There is always one more term than there are plus and minus signs.

lessons.title: Coefficients and Constants
lessons.intro: The number in front of a letter is called its coefficient. A term with no letter is called a constant.
explanation: In 7x the coefficient of x is 7.
In x + 4 the coefficient of x is 1, because x = 1 × x.
In 5y + 9 the constant is 9. It stays the same whatever y is.
lessons.rule: Coefficient: the number multiplying the letter. Constant: the number standing alone.
lessons.tip: No number in front of the letter? Then the coefficient is 1.

lessons.title: Reading an Expression
lessons.intro: Now you can read any expression aloud.
explanation: 3x + 5 reads: three times a number, plus five.
2y − 1 reads: twice a number, minus one.
x ÷ 4 reads: a number divided by four.
lessons.rule: Read the coefficient first, then the letter, then what is added or taken away.
lessons.tip: Saying an expression aloud makes word problems much easier later.

quiz.question: In the term 9x, what is the coefficient of x?
quiz.hint: The coefficient is the number written in front of the letter.

quiz.question: How many terms are there in 3x + 4y + 7?
quiz.hint: Count the parts between the plus signs.

quiz.question: What is the constant term in 6x + 11?
quiz.hint: The constant is the term with no letter.

quiz.question: What is the coefficient of y in 4x + y + 2?
quiz.hint: There is no number written in front of y. What does that mean?

quiz.question: Anil buys 4 samosas. The cost in rupees is written as a number followed by x. What is that number?
quiz.hint: Four lots of x. How do we write that?
quiz.story: A samosa costs x rupees at the school canteen.

quiz.question: Six auto-rickshaws carry 6n passengers. If n = 3, how many passengers is that?
quiz.hint: 6n means 6 times n.

quiz.question: How many terms are there in 5x + 2y − 3x + 8 − y?
quiz.hint: Count the parts between the plus and minus signs.

quiz.question: In 2x + 9y + 4, add the coefficient of x, the coefficient of y and the constant. What do you get?
quiz.hint: Pick out the three numbers first, then add them.

lessons.title: Putting a Number In
lessons.intro: To find the value of an expression, put the number in place of the letter. This is called substitution.
explanation: Find the value of 3x + 5 when x = 4.
3x means 3 times x, so 3x = 3 × 4 = 12.
Then 12 + 5 = 17. So 3x + 5 = 17 when x = 4.
lessons.rule: Replace the letter with its number, put the × sign back, then calculate.
lessons.tip: When x = 4, 3x is 3 × 4 = 12. It is not 34.

steps.text: Put 4 in place of x. Bring back the times sign.

lessons.title: Two Letters
lessons.intro: An expression can have more than one letter. Replace each one with its own value.
explanation: Find the value of 2x + 3y when x = 5 and y = 2.
lessons.rule: Replace every letter, one at a time, with its own value.
lessons.tip: Write each value above its letter before you start.

lessons.title: Multiplying Letters
lessons.intro: When letters sit side by side, multiply their values.
explanation: Find the value of xy when x = 3 and y = 4.
In the same way 2xy = 2 × 3 × 4 = 24.
lessons.rule: Letters written together are multiplied.
lessons.tip: With 3 and 4, xy is 12. It is not 34 and it is not 7.

lessons.title: Squares
lessons.intro: x² means x times x. Work out the square before anything else.
explanation: x² = x × x.
If x = 5, then x² = 5 × 5 = 25.
So x² + 1 = 25 + 1 = 26 when x = 5.
lessons.rule: x² is x times x, not x times 2.
lessons.tip: 5² = 25, but 5 × 2 = 10. They are different.

lessons.title: One Letter Depends on Another
lessons.intro: In some exam questions the value of one letter is built from another. Find them in order.
explanation: Suppose x = 7, y = x − 2 and p = y + 5.
First y = 7 − 2 = 5. Then p = 5 + 5 = 10.
Now any expression is easy: (x + y) × p = (7 + 5) × 10 = 120.
lessons.rule: Find the letters in the order they are given, then substitute.
lessons.tip: Write each new value down as soon as you find it.

steps.text: Start with the letter you know.
Now find the value of the expression.

quiz.question: Find the value of 4x + 3 when x = 5.
quiz.hint: 4x means 4 times x. Multiply first, then add.

quiz.question: Find the value of 20 − 3y when y = 4.
quiz.hint: Work out 3y first, then take it away from 20.

quiz.question: Find the value of 3x + 2y when x = 4 and y = 5.
quiz.hint: Find 3x and 2y separately, then add them.

quiz.question: Find the value of xy + 6 when x = 7 and y = 3.
quiz.hint: xy means x times y.

quiz.question: Diya's bill is 5x + 2y rupees. If x = 30 and y = 10, how many rupees is the bill?
quiz.hint: Five notebooks and two pens. Find each cost, then add.
quiz.story: A notebook costs x rupees and a pen costs y rupees.

quiz.question: Its perimeter is 2p + 2q centimetres. If p = 12 and q = 7, what is the perimeter in centimetres?
quiz.hint: Find 2p and 2q separately, then add them.
quiz.story: A rectangle has length p centimetres and width q centimetres.

quiz.question: If x = 7, y = x − 2 and p = y + 5, find the value of (p + x) × y.
quiz.hint: Find y first, then p. Work out the bracket before you multiply.

quiz.question: If x = 6, find the value of x² + 3x − 4.
quiz.hint: x² means x times x. Work that out first.

lessons.title: Like and Unlike Terms
lessons.intro: Terms with exactly the same letters are called like terms.
explanation: 3x and 5x are like terms. Both are lots of x.
3x and 5y are unlike terms. One is lots of x and the other is lots of y.
4 and 9 are like terms too, because both are plain numbers.
lessons.rule: Like terms have the same letter part.
lessons.tip: Think of x as apples and y as bananas. Apples go with apples.

lessons.title: Adding Like Terms
lessons.intro: To add like terms, add their coefficients. The letter stays the same.
explanation: Three apples and five apples make eight apples.
Check with x = 2: 3x + 5x = 6 + 10 = 16, and 8x = 16.
lessons.rule: Add the coefficients and keep the letter.
lessons.tip: x + x = 2x, because x on its own means 1x.

steps.text: Both terms are lots of x, so they are like terms.

steps.tip: The letter does not change when you add.

lessons.title: Subtracting Like Terms
lessons.intro: Subtracting works the same way. Subtract the coefficients and keep the letter.
explanation: y on its own means 1y, so 6y − y = 5y.
7x − 7x = 0. Nothing is left.
lessons.rule: Subtract the coefficients and keep the letter.
lessons.tip: A letter with no number in front has coefficient 1.

lessons.title: Collecting Mixed Terms
lessons.intro: When an expression has different kinds of terms, collect each kind separately.
explanation: Simplify 4x + 3y + 2x + 5y.
The x terms: 4x + 2x = 6x. The y terms: 3y + 5y = 8y.
So 4x + 3y + 2x + 5y = 6x + 8y. Unlike terms cannot be joined any further.
lessons.rule: Collect each kind of term separately.
lessons.tip: Underline the x terms once and the y terms twice, so you do not mix them.

steps.text: Find the x terms and add them.
Find the y terms and add them.

lessons.title: Adding Whole Expressions
lessons.intro: To add expressions, drop the brackets and collect like terms.
explanation: Add 3x + 2y − 1 and x − 2y + 4.
The x terms: 3x + x = 4x. The y terms: 2y − 2y = 0. The numbers: 4 − 1 = 3.
lessons.rule: When expressions are added, like terms from each one are collected together.
lessons.tip: Terms can cancel. 2y − 2y leaves nothing.

quiz.question: 3x + 6x simplifies to a single term. What is its coefficient?
quiz.hint: Add the coefficients and keep the letter.

quiz.question: 10y − 4y simplifies to a single term. What is its coefficient?
quiz.hint: Subtract the coefficients and keep the letter.

quiz.question: 5x + x + 2x simplifies to a single term. What is its coefficient?
quiz.hint: x on its own means 1x.

quiz.question: Simplify 7x + 2y + 3x + 6y. What is the coefficient of x in the answer?
quiz.hint: Collect only the x terms.

quiz.question: He has 4x marbles in a tin and 5x marbles in a box. If x = 6, how many marbles does he have in all?
quiz.hint: Add the like terms first, then put 6 in place of x.
quiz.story: Rohan keeps his marbles in a tin and a box.

quiz.question: Team A spends 3x + 4y rupees. Team B spends 2x + y rupees. The total is written as one expression. What is the coefficient of y in the total?
quiz.hint: Collect only the y terms. y on its own means 1y.
quiz.story: A shop sells cricket bats for x rupees and balls for y rupees.

quiz.question: Add 4x + 5y − 3, 2x − 3y + 2 and 4y − 3x + 4. What is the coefficient of y in the sum?
quiz.hint: Pick out the three y terms. Watch the minus sign on one of them.

quiz.question: Add x + y − 1, y − x + 1 and 1 − 2y. All the letters cancel. What number is left?
quiz.hint: Collect the x terms, then the y terms, then the plain numbers.

lessons.title: More Than and Less Than
lessons.intro: Words can be turned into expressions one phrase at a time.
explanation: 5 more than x is written x + 5.
3 less than x is written x − 3.
Take care with the order. 3 less than x is x − 3, not 3 − x.
lessons.rule: More than means add. Less than means subtract from the letter.
lessons.tip: Try a number. If x is 10, then 3 less than x is 7. Check: 10 − 3 = 7.

lessons.title: Times and Shared
lessons.intro: Other words point to multiplying and dividing.
explanation: Twice x, or double x, is 2x.
The product of 4 and y is 4y.
x shared equally among 3 is x ÷ 3.
lessons.rule: Twice, double, product and times mean multiply. Shared and each mean divide.
lessons.tip: Half of x is x ÷ 2.

lessons.title: Two Steps in Words
lessons.intro: Longer phrases are built up step by step.
explanation: '5 more than twice x' is built in two steps.
Twice x is 2x. Then 5 more gives 2x + 5.
'Twice the sum of x and 5' is different: 2(x + 5) = 2x + 10.
lessons.rule: Follow the words in order, one step at a time.
lessons.tip: The words 'the sum of' need brackets.

steps.text: Check with 3 in place of x. Twice 3 is 6, and 5 more is 11.

lessons.title: Totals from Stories
lessons.intro: Stories with two kinds of things need two terms.
explanation: Arnav sends m messages each hour for 5 hours. That is 5m messages.
Pranav sends p messages each hour for 4 hours. That is 4p messages.
Together they send 5m + 4p messages. The two terms are unlike, so they stay separate.
lessons.rule: Make one term for each kind of thing, then add the terms.
lessons.tip: 5m + 4p is not 9mp. Only like terms can be joined.

lessons.title: Numbers in a Row
lessons.intro: Numbers that follow each other can share one letter.
explanation: If a number is n, the next number is n + 1.
Odd numbers go up in twos: 5, 7, 9. So if an odd number is n, the next odd number is n + 2.
The sum of two odd numbers in a row is n + (n + 2) = 2n + 2.
lessons.rule: Next number: add 1. Next odd number or next even number: add 2.
lessons.tip: Test your expression with a real number to be sure.

steps.text: Call the first odd number n. The next odd number is 2 more.
Suppose the question says the sum is 12.
steps.tip: This is true when n = 5, because 5 + 7 = 12.

quiz.question: 8 more than x is written x + 8. What is its value when x = 12?
quiz.hint: Put 12 in place of x.

quiz.question: Twice a number n, minus 3, is written 2n − 3. What is its value when n = 10?
quiz.hint: Work out 2n first.

quiz.question: '5 more than three times x' is written as an expression. What is its value when x = 4?
quiz.hint: Three times x comes first. Then add 5.

quiz.question: 'Twice the sum of x and 5' is written as an expression. What is its value when x = 4?
quiz.hint: Find the sum in the brackets first, then double it.

quiz.question: Arnav sends m messages each hour for 5 hours. Pranav sends p messages each hour for 4 hours. If m = 6 and p = 10, how many messages do they send in all?
quiz.hint: The total is 5m + 4p. Find each term, then add.
quiz.story: Arnav and Pranav are sending messages on Saturday afternoon.

quiz.question: Mangoes cost x rupees each and bananas cost y rupees each. Sana buys 3 mangoes and 12 bananas. If x = 25 and y = 5, how many rupees does she pay?
quiz.hint: The cost is 3x + 12y. Find each term, then add.
quiz.story: Sana is buying fruit at a market in Lucknow.

quiz.question: The sum of two odd numbers in a row is 16. If the smaller one is n, then n + (n + 2) = 16. What is n?
quiz.hint: The two numbers are 2 apart. Take 2 from the sum, then halve.

quiz.question: Three numbers in a row add up to 48. If the smallest is n, the sum is n + (n + 1) + (n + 2). What is n?
quiz.hint: The sum is three lots of n and 3 more. Take the 3 away first.

lessons.title: A Number Times a Term
lessons.intro: To multiply a term by a number, multiply the coefficient. The letter stays.
explanation: Three lots of 2x make 6x.
Check with x = 5: 2x = 10, and 3 × 10 = 30. Also 6x = 30.
lessons.rule: To multiply a term by a number, multiply the coefficient.
lessons.tip: 4 × 5y = 20y. The y just comes along.

lessons.title: A Number Times a Bracket
lessons.intro: A number outside a bracket multiplies every term inside.
explanation: The 2 multiplies the x, and it also multiplies the 3.
lessons.rule: Multiply every term inside the bracket by the number outside.
lessons.tip: Draw an arrow from the outside number to each term inside.

steps.text: Multiply the first term in the bracket.

steps.tip: Both terms are multiplied, not just the first.

lessons.title: Dividing a Term
lessons.intro: Dividing undoes multiplying. Divide the numbers, and cancel any letter that is in both.
explanation: 12xy ÷ 4y = 3x. The y on top and the y below cancel.
Check with x = 2 and y = 5: 12xy = 120 and 4y = 20, and 120 ÷ 20 = 6. Also 3x = 6.
lessons.rule: Divide the coefficients and cancel the letters that match.
lessons.tip: A letter divided by itself is 1, so it disappears.

steps.text: Cancel the y that is in both.

lessons.title: Dividing a Sum
lessons.intro: To divide a sum, divide each term.
explanation: In (12xy + 8y) ÷ 4y, both terms are divided by 4y.
12xy ÷ 4y = 3x and 8y ÷ 4y = 2.
lessons.rule: Divide every term of the sum by the divisor.
lessons.tip: It is the reverse of multiplying a bracket: 4y(3x + 2) = 12xy + 8y.

lessons.title: Testing a Statement
lessons.intro: Some exam questions give a value and ask which statement is true. Work out both sides.
explanation: Is 5x + 6 = 7x − 8 true when x = 7?
Left side: 5 × 7 + 6 = 41. Right side: 7 × 7 − 8 = 41.
Both sides come to 41, so the statement is true when x is 7.
lessons.rule: A statement is true for a value when both sides come out equal.
lessons.tip: Work out each side separately. Do not move terms across.

steps.text: Put 7 in place of x on the left side.
Put 7 in place of x on the right side.

steps.tip: They match, so the statement is true.

quiz.question: 5 × 3x simplifies to a single term. What is its coefficient?
quiz.hint: Multiply the two numbers. The letter stays.

quiz.question: 3(x + 4) is written without brackets as 3x plus a number. What is the number?
quiz.hint: The 3 multiplies the 4 as well as the x.

quiz.question: 20xy ÷ 5y simplifies to a single term. What is its coefficient?
quiz.hint: Divide the numbers. The y cancels.

quiz.question: (15xy + 10y) ÷ 5y simplifies to 3x plus a number. What is the number?
quiz.hint: Divide each term by 5y. Look at the second term.

quiz.question: A fence goes all the way round, so it would be 4x metres long. A gate takes up 2 metres, so the fence is 4x − 2 metres. If x = 9, how long is the fence in metres?
quiz.hint: Work out 4x first, then take away the gate.
quiz.story: A square garden has sides of x metres.

quiz.question: The cake costs 6x rupees and the sweets cost 9 rupees, so each friend pays (6x + 9) ÷ 3 rupees. If x = 20, how many rupees does each friend pay?
quiz.hint: Find the total cost first, then share it among three.
quiz.story: Three friends share the cost of a cake and a box of sweets equally.

quiz.question: When x is 6, the value of 12x − 14 is the same as the value of 7x + 16. What is that value?
quiz.hint: Put 6 in place of x in either expression. You can use the other one to check.

quiz.question: If x = 7 and y = 2x − 9, find the value of 4y − 2x.
quiz.hint: Find y first. Then work out 4y and 2x.
